product: Seamless and welded steel pipe - OCTG casing and tubing, plus offshore line pipe - for oil and gas drilling, sold via Rig Direct. Demand comes from drilling activity in US and Canada shales, Argentina Vaca Muerta (42 rigs), deepwater offshore (Cronos, Sakarya, GranMorgu) and the Middle East. (GlobeNewswire 2026-08-05)
demand: Price-led. H1 2026 sales +1% to $6,067M on tube volumes -1% and average selling prices +2%, driven by North America price increases (GlobeNewswire 2026-08-05). In Q2 the 4% decline was volume-driven with ASPs flat. Q4 2026 is expected to add both volume and pricing. (transcript 2026-08-06)
pricing_power: Q2 2026 EBITDA margin already fell to 21.9% from 23.7% on higher unitary logistics costs, lower fixed-cost absorption and rising raw-material costs (GlobeNewswire 2026-08-05). A prolonged Hormuz closure cutting premium upper-Gulf mix, further hot-rolled coil inflation, or higher US Section 232 tariff costs would compress margins further.
competition: Chinese seamless OCTG producers (Baoshan, TPCO, Hengyang Valin) are the low-cost substitute; imported OCTG is the stated competitive threat, currently held back by US Section 232 tariffs. On the 2026-08-06 call management flagged import parity as US Pipe Logix prices (already +9% YTD) rise further. (transcript 2026-08-06)
market_strategy: CEO Gabriel Podskubka (2026-08-05/06 call): H2 2026 sales and EBITDA in line with H1; Q3 weakest, with an important jump of volume and some pricing in Q4. The $130M upper-Gulf backlog is upside if Hormuz reopens (70-90 days). Board committed to shareholder returns broadly in line with past practice: one-third interim, two-thirds in May. (transcript 2026-08-06)
bull: Q2 2026 EPS $0.95 beat $0.82 and revenue $2.97B beat $2.94B (2026-08-05); H1 sales +1% to $6,067M, net cash $3.6B, dividend doubled to $0.59/sh; US Pipe Logix +9% YTD with 50 rigs added and Q4 volume/pricing jump guided.
bear: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 21.9% from 23.7% on Hormuz logistics costs; sales -4% y/y; $130M Gulf backlog excluded from H2 base case; three of four 90-day analyst actions were lowers or downgrades; 21-day momentum +3% is context only.
falsifier: Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-04: EBITDA materially below Q2 2026 EBITDA of $649M, or H2 2026 sales/EBITDA below H1's $6,067M/$1,385M, proves the in-line guidance and bull case wrong.

web_bottleneck: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz: the closure postponed deliveries to Iraq, Kuwait and Qatar, stranding $130M of premium-grade material and raising unitary logistics costs (GlobeNewswire 2026-08-05; transcript 2026-08-06). The company constraint is raw-material hot-rolled coil and freight cost inflation reducing fixed-cost absorption.
web_who_benefits_next: US, Canadian and Argentine shale drillers; Middle East NOCs still drilling (Aramco in Saudi Arabia, ADNOC in UAE maintained activity); offshore operators Eni and TotalEnergies (Cronos, Sakarya), TotalEnergies (GranMorgu, Suriname); YPF and the Argentina LNG project. Second-order: Ternium (TX) via equity earnings. (transcript 2026-08-06)
web_who_loses: Imported-OCTG competitors and their exporters, notably Vallourec and Chinese mill exporters, lose share in the tariff-protected US market; any pipe supplier displaced by Tenaris offshore and Rig Direct wins loses too. Customers pay higher OCTG prices as Pipe Logix rises. (transcript 2026-08-06)
